correctness.rationale: For t_(g,A) after t_(h,B) the domain is B∩h^(-1)A; the reverse has domain A∩g^(-1)B. If h≠1, the event B_x=1, A_x=0, A_(hx)=1 forces a domain disagreement for every g and has probability 1/8 under independent uniform Boolean domains. The h-cycles have length ℓ=ord(h)≥2 and disjoint adjacent edges of total count (n/ℓ) floor(ℓ/2)≥n/3; the tested membership bits on these edges are independent. This bounds each raw label count by 4^n(7/8)^(n/3); swap the maps when only g is nontrivial. The identity label count is exactly 4^n. Nonempty restrictions uniquely determine their labels by regularity, and all empty restrictions represent a single zero. The upper bound follows already by assigning the actual zero the identity label to inject all actual pairs into the raw count; the exact correction in the original also checks, since n²(2^(n+1)-1)-(2N-1)=2n(n-1)2^n-(n-1)². The partial identities give the lower bound and the claimed conditional share. Dividing by N²=n²4^n(1-(1-1/n)2^(-n))² yields the uniform relative asymptotic with the specified θ; n=1 gives K=4 exactly. Independently reproduced the six finite examples by factoring raw domain counts over the orbits of the subgroup generated by the two labels, and checked the raw bound via an exact integer inequality. In the noncommuting-label case the two compositions have to be both empty, since ghx≠hgx everywhere; this was imposed in the replay but is not needed for the abstract upper bound.
residual_risks: The finite replay does not prove the infinite-family bound; the matching proof supplies it. Neither the exponential constant's optimality nor applicability to nonregular actions is claimed.

value.rationale: The result explains why the full monoid commuting probability is asymptotically inverse square in group order regardless of the multiplication law: almost every commuting pair consists of partial identities. The missing two-nonidentity sector is not a normalization check or a direct use of the group commuting probability. A uniform explicit bound makes the concentration precise even over arbitrary changing families of finite groups.
residual_risks: The theorem does not give the exact count for every group or sharp exponential rate.
